place.en: The hidden realm · The cliff wall

setup.zh: 头顶传来脚步声。马小宝和那五个人，顺着崖壁爬下来：「秘境里死个把人，可不稀奇。」
setup.en: Footsteps overhead. Ma Xiaobao and his five come climbing down the cliff. "People die in the hidden realm all the time."

recap.zh: 马小宝六个人追下崖来，你踩了一脚那块长得像马小宝的石头——六个人像壁虎一样粘在了崖壁上，三天后才开。
recap.en: Ma Xiaobao and his five came down the cliff after you; you stepped on the stone that looked like Ma Xiaobao — and the six of them stuck to the cliff like geckos, not to come free for three days.

zh: 崖壁上，亮起一圈淡淡的光。
六个人，像六只壁虎，贴在崖壁上。
en: A faint ring of light glows on the cliff.
Six people stuck to the rock like six geckos.
"It opens by itself in three days."

story.zh:
便在这时，头顶上传来一阵脚步声，碎石子一阵一阵往下落。

「——我就说他往这边走了！」

小满抬头一看，崖顶上站着一排人，不多不少，正好六个。当中那个胖墩墩的，身上的新法衣在黑地里也看得出是簇新的，正是马小宝。他身后五个，便是柴房那天夜里的五个，卖地图的那两个也在里头。马小宝一只手叉着腰，一只手捏着半块桂花糕，居高临下，笑得很是开心：「沈小满。右边人多，我当你往哪儿钻了呢。原来你是个识货的——那面墙，开了？」

小满站在墙前，没有说话。

马小宝把那半块桂花糕塞进嘴里，一边嚼，一边道：「秘境里头，死个把人，可不稀奇。十年前粘住三个，疯了一个。今年嘛——」他回头冲那五个人一扬下巴，「——多一个沈小满，谁也不会多问一句。」说罢，领着五个人，顺着崖壁往下爬。

六个人一齐往下爬，崖壁上碎石子哗啦啦地响。小满心里飞快地算了一遍：六个人，五个老弟子，练气三层的两个，二层的三个；马小宝练气一层——这一个多月又吃了多少丹药，不好说。自己练气三层。柴房那天夜里是二层，这二十来天，夜夜在柴房后头吐纳，木牌夜夜是暖的，暖得他一口气能在经脉里转上三周，三天前的夜里，冲开了第三层。打得过么？也许打得过。可打过了，六个人回去一说，全外门便都知道了：一个进门两个来月、下下之资的五行杂灵根，一个人在秘境里打翻了六个。那便藏不住了。

他正算着，肩膀上的银月打了个哈欠。

这哈欠打得又长又慢，打完了，它才懒洋洋地道：「……往左边那块石头上，踩一下。」

小满问：「哪块？」

银月道：「那块长得像马小宝的。」

小满低头往墙脚下一看，一眼便找着了。那石头又圆又胖，圆得不讲道理，胖得理直气壮，上头还长着一小撮青苔，正好长在「脑门」上，活像马小宝戴着他那顶小帽。小满心想，天底下竟有这般像的石头，也不知是石头长得像马小宝，还是马小宝长得像石头。他没有再想下去，抬起脚，一脚踩了上去。

那石头往下一沉。

崖壁上登时亮起一圈淡淡的光，青白青白的，从崖脚一直亮到崖顶，像是有人拿一支极大的笔，在那面崖上画了一个圈。圈一亮，正往下爬的六个人，同时停住了——不是自己要停，是动不了了。一个个手脚张开，贴在崖壁上，像六只给粘在墙上的壁虎，手指头还扒在石缝里，脚尖还蹬在石棱上，身子却像是给什么东西钉住了，任他们怎么挣，怎么蹬，就是挪不动半分。

马小宝贴在最当中，脸朝着崖壁，只能拿眼角往下斜着看，叫道：「你——你干了什么！」

小满道：「我什么都没干。」

这话说得一点也不假。他只是踩了一块石头，一块长得像马小宝的石头。踩一块石头，算不得干了什么。

马小宝又叫：「放开！放开我！」

银月在小满肩膀上又打了个哈欠，道：「前人留下的困阵。护着这面墙的。石门合上前半个时辰，自己就开了。」

小满便仰起头来，好心转告：「小宝哥，这是前人留下的阵。关门前半个时辰，自己就开了。」

马小宝愣了一愣，脑子里慢慢地算了一笔账——他平日算账不大灵，这一笔却算得飞快——算完了，一声惨叫，在崖壁上撞来撞去：「那不是三天？！三天！我——我还没吃早饭！」

五个跟班里有一个也叫起来：「马师兄，你刚才吃了桂花糕——」

马小宝道：「那是早饭前的！」

马小宝在崖上挣了半天，挣得满头大汗，眼见挣不脱，脸上那点凶相便一点一点地化了，化成了另一副模样。他咽了一口唾沫，声音软了下来：「沈……沈师弟。」

小满道：「小宝哥。」

马小宝道：「咱们一个村出来的。」

小满道：「是。」

马小宝道：「你把我们放下来。我……我给你十两银子。」

小满道：「我放不下来。这是前人的阵。」

马小宝道：「二十两！」

小满道：「小宝哥，前人的阵，不收银子。」

马小宝憋了半天，道：「那……那公中，往后你不用交了。」

小满想了一想，道：「这个好。小宝哥，你记着。」

马小宝道：「我记着！」

小满道：「我也记着。」他从怀里摸出那个红糖包纸订的小本子，借着崖壁上那一圈青白的光，舔了舔笔尖，写道：**冬月初一。左崖。马小宝许：公中免交。**写完了，他抬起头来，很诚恳地道：「可我还是放不下来。」

马小宝那张脸，贴在崖壁上，慢慢地，变成了他爹的那种颜色。

这一笔许诺，后来到了腊月初一，马小宝照样坐在那只描金小木匣后头，照样拿指节笃笃地敲着匣子，照样道：「沈小满。两块。」小满照样交了，交完了，翻到本子上冬月初一那一行，在底下添了两个字：**未兑。**
story.en:
Just then footsteps sounded overhead, and gravel came trickling down in bursts.

"— I told you he went this way!"

Xiaoman looked up. On the cliff top stood a row of men, exactly six. The chubby one in the middle, his new robe plainly brand-new even in the dark, was Ma Xiaobao. Behind him, the five from that night at the woodshed; the two map-sellers among them. Ma Xiaobao stood hand on hip, half an osmanthus cake in the other hand, looking down and grinning very happily: "Shen Xiaoman. More people on the right — I wondered where you'd burrowed. So you know a good thing when you see it — that wall, it's open?"

Xiaoman stood before the wall and said nothing.

Ma Xiaobao stuffed the half cake into his mouth and said as he chewed, "In the hidden realm people die now and then. Nothing strange in it. Ten years ago it stuck three, one went mad. This year —" he jerked his chin back at the five — "— one more Shen Xiaoman, nobody asks a thing." With that he led the five down the cliff.

Six men climbing down at once; the gravel rattled. Xiaoman ran the sums fast: six men, five old disciples, two at the third level, three at the second; Ma Xiaobao at the first — how many more pills he'd eaten this month and more, hard to say. Himself: the third level. The night of the woodshed he'd been at the second; these twenty-odd days he'd breathed behind the woodshed every night, the token warm every night, warm enough that one breath went three times round his channels, and three nights ago he'd broken into the third. Could he beat them? Perhaps. But beat them, and the six go back and tell, and the whole outer court knows: a mixed five-element root, bottom of the bottom, two months in, flattened six by himself in the hidden realm. Then there'd be no hiding.

As he was reckoning, Yinyue on his shoulder yawned.

A long, slow yawn; only when it was done did it say lazily: "…Step on that stone on the left."

"Which?"

"The one that looks like Ma Xiaobao."

Xiaoman looked down at the foot of the wall and found it at once. Round and fat — round beyond reason, fat and unashamed of it — with a little tuft of moss growing right on its "forehead," just like Ma Xiaobao in his little cap. Xiaoman thought: that such a likeness should exist in the world — whether the stone looks like Ma Xiaobao or Ma Xiaobao like the stone, who can say. He thought no further, lifted his foot, and stepped on it.

The stone sank.

At once a ring of faint light lit up on the cliff face, bluish white, from the foot of the cliff to its top, as if someone had taken a very great brush and drawn a circle on it. The moment the circle lit, the six climbing down all stopped at once — not by choice; they could not move. Each one spread-eagled against the cliff like six geckos stuck to a wall, fingers still hooked in cracks, toes still on ledges, bodies as if nailed there; strain and kick as they might, not an inch.

Ma Xiaobao, stuck in the very middle, face to the rock, could only squint down from the corner of his eye. "You — what did you do!"

"Nothing," said Xiaoman.

Not a word of a lie. He had only stepped on a stone — a stone that looked like Ma Xiaobao. Stepping on a stone is not doing anything.

"Let go! Let me go!" Ma Xiaobao yelled.

On Xiaoman's shoulder Yinyue yawned again. "A binding the old ones left. Guards this wall. Half an hour before the stone door shuts, it opens by itself."

So Xiaoman looked up and passed it on kindly: "Brother Xiaobao, it's a binding the old ones left. Half an hour before the door shuts, it opens by itself."

Ma Xiaobao went blank, then slowly worked out a sum in his head — ordinarily his sums were poor, but this one he did very fast — and when it was done let out a scream that bounced back and forth off the cliff: "That's three days?! Three days! I — I haven't had breakfast!"

One of the five cried too: "Brother Ma, you just had osmanthus cake —"

"That was before breakfast!"

Ma Xiaobao strained on the cliff a long while, sweating, and when he saw he couldn't break loose the fierceness melted off his face bit by bit into another look entirely. He swallowed, and his voice went soft: "Sh… Brother Shen."

"Brother Xiaobao," said Xiaoman.

"We're from the same village."

"We are."

"Get us down. I'll… I'll give you ten taels of silver."

"I can't get you down. It's the old ones' binding."

"Twenty taels!"

"Brother Xiaobao, the old ones' binding doesn't take silver."

Ma Xiaobao held it in a long while, then said, "Then… the common fund — you needn't pay it any more."

Xiaoman thought, and said, "That's good. Brother Xiaobao, you remember that."

"I'll remember!"

"So will I." He took out the little notebook sewn from red-sugar paper, and by the bluish-white ring on the cliff licked his brush and wrote: **First day, eleventh month. Left cliff. Ma Xiaobao promises: no more common fund.** Then he looked up and said very sincerely, "But I still can't get you down."

Ma Xiaobao's face, pressed to the rock, slowly turned his father's colour.

As for that promise: when the first of the twelfth month came, Ma Xiaobao sat behind the little gilt box as before, rapped it with his knuckle as before, and said as before, "Shen Xiaoman. Two." Xiaoman paid as before, and afterwards turned to the line for the first of the eleventh month and added two characters beneath it: **Not honoured.**

exits.means: throws a radish up to Ma Xiaobao

refuse.en: You have no radish on you.

story.zh:
小满站在崖底下，仰着头，看着那六只壁虎。他想了一想，从包袱里摸出一根萝卜。

这萝卜，是伙房那位大娘给的。自从上回他拿萝卜去药园「练功」，那位大娘便认准了这孩子练的是一门吃萝卜的功夫，每回见他，都要往他怀里塞一根，这一回听说他要进秘境，一口气塞了三根，还叮嘱他：「秘境里头冷，萝卜是暖的。」

小满掂了掂那根萝卜，往上一扔。

那萝卜在半空里划了一道弧线，翻了两个筋斗，不偏不倚，正落进马小宝张大的嘴里，「噗」的一声，塞了个严严实实。

小满说道：「利息。」

他包袱里还剩一根萝卜。他摸了一摸，没有再扔。利息只给一回；给两回，那便不是利息，是本钱了。本钱，是要他们自己还的。

说罢，他转过身去，走进了那道墙。

身后，马小宝「呜呜呜」地叫了半天，叫的是什么，谁也听不清。小满走了几步，忽然想起一件事来：三天，没有水，六个人会不会渴死？他回头望了一望，只见那道崖壁虽是死的，崖顶上却有水一滴一滴地渗下来，正好顺着崖面往下淌，淌过马小宝的额头，淌过他的鼻尖，淌到那根萝卜上。他这才放了心，心想：前人留这个阵，倒也不是要人的命，只是要人在那里挂着，想一想。

至于想什么，他不知道。马小宝多半也不知道。
story.en:
Xiaoman stood at the foot of the cliff, head back, looking at the six geckos. He thought a moment, and took a radish from his bundle.

The radish came from the big auntie in the kitchen. Since the time he took radishes to the herb garden to "practise," she had decided the boy practised some radish-eating art, and whenever she saw him pushed one into his coat; hearing this time that he was off to the hidden realm, she pushed in three at a go and told him: "It's cold in the hidden realm. Radishes are warm."

Xiaoman weighed the radish in his hand and tossed it up.

It drew an arc through the air, turned two somersaults, and dropped neither left nor right but straight into Ma Xiaobao's gaping mouth — pop — and plugged it tight.

"Interest," said Xiaoman.

There was one radish left in his bundle. He felt it, and didn't throw it. Interest is paid once; paid twice, it isn't interest any more, it's principal. Principal they had to pay back themselves.

With that he turned and walked into the wall.

Behind him Ma Xiaobao went "mmf-mmf-mmf" a long while — what he was saying, nobody could make out. Xiaoman had gone a few steps when something occurred to him: three days without water — would the six die of thirst? He looked back, and saw that though the cliff was dead, water seeped down from the top a drop at a time, running down the face — over Ma Xiaobao's forehead, over the tip of his nose. Only then was he easy, and thought: the old ones didn't leave this binding to kill anybody — only to hang a man there a while, to think.

Think about what, he didn't know. Ma Xiaobao most likely didn't either.

exits.means: leaves them stuck and goes through the wall

story.en:
Xiaoman stood at the foot of the cliff, head back, looking at the six geckos. He felt the radish in his bundle, thought a moment, and in the end didn't take it out. Interest is a funny thing: sometimes not giving it is a way of giving.

He turned and walked into the wall.

Behind him Ma Xiaobao went "mmf-mmf-mmf" a long while — what he was saying, nobody could make out. Xiaoman had gone a few steps when something occurred to him: three days without water — would the six die of thirst? He looked back, and saw that though the cliff was dead, water seeped down from the top a drop at a time, running down the face — over Ma Xiaobao's forehead, over the tip of his nose. Only then was he easy, and thought: the old ones didn't leave this binding to kill anybody — only to hang a man there a while, to think.

Think about what, he didn't know. Ma Xiaobao most likely didn't either.
